label: early "i" after "d" in a u-rich / p-initial prefix
explanation: Very sparse (56 activations across 1M sequences), all in the original-input phase at t=3..6 (most at t=4). It fires almost only on the input i (84% of mass); the few other tokens it fires on (u, m, n, q, j) have similar prefixes. The prefix matters a lot: the previous token is usually d, an earlier u is almost always present, and the sequence often starts with p (q, u, b also occur). The strongest activations are i right after d with u repeated earlier (b u u u d i = max, q u u d i, p u 2 0 d i). Weak activations are i after prefixes with only some of these parts (p t u p m i, p u t c i). It never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, at t<3, or at t>=7. Plain i after d with a u earlier gives low precision (~5-8%), so the feature needs the conjunction (two or more u, or a p start). The predicate is precise (~86% dev) but misses about 40% of mass, where parts of the conjunction are absent. This looks like a narrow lookup on a specific prefix rather than a clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 12 cues. Raise it: orig0=p (+2.90), orig1=u (+2.29), prev_tok=d (+1.92), prev3_tok=u (+1.74), orig2=u (+1.55), phase=0 & in_tok=i (+1.39). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.14), prev3_tok=- (-1.54), orig7=- (-0.96).
